title: Rabbi Abba bar Mimi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 1, on Naavu [compare 1:10:2], mentions him favorably when describing scholars engaging with one another over halakhah, such as Rabbi Abba bar Mimi and his colleagues. Hyman says they are not found elsewhere. R' Yerucham Leiner, in Seder HaDorot HaShalem, suggests that Rosh Hashanah 35a, “When R' Abba came up from the sea,” should instead read bar Mimi.

notes.text: The supplied מייללין remains lexically uncertain; the rendering gives the broad activity without deciding whether it means disputing, sharpening or another form of discussion. Rashi explains Rosh Hashanah35a מימי as returning from a sea voyage; Leiner instead proposes the patronym bar Mimi. The proposed identification remains open.

The saved whole TE ShirHaShirimRabbah1:10:2 scalar explicitly names full Rabbi Abba barMimi with colleagues engaging over halakhah. It locates the Naavu passage, but vocalized מייללין does not itself settle the exact activity or prove a simple lexical derivation. Hyman’s not-found-elsewhere statement remains his search claim, not a fresh global absence conclusion. The earlier Rashi sea-voyage explanation at RoshHashanah35a is inherited, while Leiner’s possible SHOULD-READ barMimi remains conjectural; no identity is admitted.

Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:10:2 names Rabbi Abba bar Mimi and his colleagues as examples of scholars exploring halakhah together. Rosh Hashanah 35a has מימי, which Rashi explains as Rabbi Abba’s return from a voyage at sea. Hyman attributes the proposed wording bar Mimi to Leiner. Both that suggestion and the exact sense of the midrash’s verb remain open.
